records.supported_name_scope: Rio Pindaré supports the representative identity of the selected river group, within the wider Mearim drainage. The eastern Rio Zutiua contribution retains separate scope. The candidate is not a uniform name for every selected reach, an exact headwater or confluence boundary, or a name for the downstream Mearim and coastal waters.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The entire three-piece modeled mainstem and separate eastern contribution were compared with the original IBGE state map, readable upper-to-lower corridor enlargements and the SEMA station inventory. The long northward upper trunk, northeast bend past Buriticupu, eastward middle section, eastern tributary junction and northeast lower continuation distinguish this Pindaré group from the adjacent Gurupi, Tocantins, Grajaú and Mearim trunks.
records.region: Western Maranhão, Brazil: the upper Pindaré west of Amarante do Maranhão, the Buriticupu and Alto Alegre do Pindaré corridor, and the lower river through Pindaré-Mirim and Monção toward the Mearim junction setting.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded representative-system correspondence across all four selected fragments. Generalized source scale leaves precise headwater naming limits, tributary-name transition vertices and the final confluence vertex unassigned; these do not prevent the representative finding.

naming_scope_details.upper_scope: Upper Pindaré corridor correspondence is supported; an exact spring, headwater endpoint or first named vertex is not assigned.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: Rio Zutiua is retained as the distinct eastern contributing corridor. The map and federal text support this name form, but it is not a whole-group alternative and is not extended to every tributary vertex.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: The group ends in the inland Pindaré–Mearim junction setting. No downstream Mearim, Baía de São Marcos, coastal extension, estuary or tidal-limit name is applied to the selected group.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The four display fragments, three modeled-mainstem pieces and generalized plotted lengths do not define natural river-name boundaries or measured river lengths. Identity is based on the whole mapped route and tributary relationships, not a bounding box, MAIN_RIV membership or the nearest label. Formal naming history, aliases and Korean translation remain unassigned.

records.supported_name_scope: Rivière Broadback supports the representative identity of the connected corridor. The modeled upper mainstem follows the Assinica contributing branch and its lake chain, rather than the separately mapped upper Broadback toward Lac Frotet. Broadback is therefore not a uniform name for all selected coordinates.
records.geographic_disambiguation: All three selected mainstem pieces were read as one route against original provincial conservation cartography. The upper southwest lake-chain approach, Assinica junction, westward Broadback trunk, northward Evans–Giffard passage and lower westward approach between Rupert and Nottaway jointly support the representative system identity.
records.region: Eeyou Istchee Baie-James, Nord-du-Québec, Canada: eastern Assinica drainage, the Broadback trunk through the Evans–Giffard setting, and Rupert Bay.
records.completion_scope: Completed for bounded representative-system correspondence. The headward feeder remains unnamed; precise lake-entry, confluence and estuarine boundary vertices are not assigned. This does not prevent identification of the connected Broadback system. The denied optional Cree conservation plan remains stopped and is not needed for the final evidence.

naming_scope_details.upper_scope: Eastern Assinica contributing drainage and Opataca–Cachisca–Comencho–Assinica lake chain; initial small feeder unassigned. The separately mapped Frotet–Labeau upper Broadback corridor is not substituted for the actual modeled headward route.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: Rivière Assinica retains its tributary identity. Coigne and Théodat are neighboring contributing-basin context, not aliases or additional selected pieces. This object has three modeled mainstem pieces and no separately selected gray tributary piece.
naming_scope_details.lake_scope: The named lake passages retain distinct waterbody names; a system-level label does not make them river-only reaches.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Lower Broadback to Rupert Bay context supported, with Rupert and Nottaway separate. No individual tidal distributary or precise marine limit assigned.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Rendered model length is not the official natural-river length, and modeled mainstem membership does not establish a continuous official hydronym. No formal naming date, Indigenous-name equivalence or historical alias sequence was established.

records.supported_name_scope: Colville River is the representative identity of the five-fragment group. Its modeled mainstem begins along Awuna River, a separately named tributary. The western non-mainstem corridor includes a Thunder Creek approach and upper Colville; delta branches and initial feeder endpoints are not assigned a uniform hydronym.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The complete northern and southern western approaches, their junction, the eastward foothills course, the Killik-area turn, Umiat, the long northward coastal-plain reach and the Nuiqsut delta setting were compared with readable original BLM cartography. Alaska is an editorial qualifier distinguishing other Colville rivers.
records.region: North Slope, Alaska, United States: northern Brooks Range foothills to the Colville delta and Harrison Bay.
records.completion_scope: Completed representative-system correspondence for all five selected fragments using two acquired original maps, supplemented by a distinct BLM hydrology report. Unassigned short feeder and delta-channel details do not prevent this bounded conclusion. No further source acquisition is pending.

naming_scope_details.upper_scope: Awuna is the modeled mainstem's western approach. Thunder Creek and upper Colville occupy the longer western non-mainstem corridor. Exact initial source points and name-transition vertices remain unassigned.
naming_scope_details.tributary_scope: The model's mainstem and tributary roles differ from natural hydronym boundaries; neither label automatically establishes the name of a complete fragment. Nuka, Kiligwa, Kuna, Ipnavik, Etivluk, Killik and other adjoining waterways remain distinct.
naming_scope_details.lake_scope: Mapped nearby lakes and floodplain waters are context only. No named lake is adopted as the source, as a river alias or as a necessary through-lake section.
naming_scope_details.terminal_scope: Colville delta and Harrison Bay association is supported. Exact branch selection, distributary-name boundaries, shoreline and present mouth remain outside this representative-system finding.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: Displayed model lengths are not surveyed named-river lengths. No current discharge, channel condition, infrastructure status, land-access right or administrative designation is inferred from historical maps.

records.supported_name_scope: No natural river identity is established for the complete modeled Inland Ice path. This completed feature-class and naming-scope hold does not claim that every nearby marginal stream is unnamed.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Northern Greenland Inland Ice, extending north from the interior into the ice-margin and inner Victoria Fjord regional setting. The fjord is location and feature-class context only, not an assigned river name.
records.completion_scope: Readable coverage supports the completed scope hold. Positive natural-river identity evidence would be required before any later name assignment; no further acquisition is pending now.

naming_scope_details.length_limit: Model display length, not a measured natural-river length.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Keep the saved order unchanged and use later result IDs/status changes to mark progress. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated; no lake research until all river continental phases have had their review pass.
